claim: Madrid totals 31 Michelin-starred restaurants in the 2026 Michelin Guide Spain, with DiverXO holding 3 stars and six restaurants holding 2 stars.
quote: One city, 31 stars: Madrid's Michelin route 2026. DiverXO retains its three stars; Deessa, Smoked Room, Paco Roncero, DSTAgE, Coque and Ramón Freixa Atelier all hold two stars.

claim: DiverXO requires a non-refundable €450 per-person ticket purchased on a 90-day rolling calendar to reserve, deducted from the final bill.
quote: To make a reservation at DiverXO, it is necessary to purchase a ticket priced at €450 (VAT included) per person... Each day, at 00:00 hours, a new date in the 2026 calendar is enabled with 90 days' notice.

claim: DiverXO (chef Dabiz Muñoz) is Madrid's only 3-star restaurant, an avant-garde Asian-influenced tasting menu in the Chamartín district.
quote: DiverXO is a Three Stars: Exceptional cuisine restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide España. Chef Dabiz Muñoz.

claim: Deessa, Quique Dacosta's 2-star restaurant inside the Mandarin Oriental Ritz (Jerónimos / Barrio de Salamanca area), serves a Contemporáneo QD menu at €195 and includes a smaller weekday Chronos format.
quote: Celebrated chef Quique Dacosta brings his unique culinary talent to Mandarin Oriental Ritz, Madrid, at Deessa... Menú Contemporáneo QD Ritz 195 €.

claim: Smoked Room by Dani García (Hyatt Regency Hesperia, Paseo de la Castellana) is a 14-seat 2-star fire-omakase with menus from €150 to €250, plus a €500 Jū ni pairing; booking opens monthly only for the current calendar month.
quote: Smoked Room... 14 guests, six at the bar and eight in the dining room... Menu options and prices include offerings starting at 150€ per person, 220€ per person, 250€ per person, and the premium 'Jū ni' pairing at 500€ per person.

claim: Coque (Sandoval brothers, Chamberí) is a 2-star sequential-spaces tasting experience with a flagship menu around €365.
quote: Coque is located in the Chamberí district... The average price for dining at Coque by Mario Sandoval should be around €365.

claim: Paco Roncero Restaurante (Centro, Casino de Madrid building near Puerta del Sol) offers three 2-star menus: Essence (€190), Madrid Madrid Madrid (€240), and Grand Madrid (€310).
quote: Grand Madrid Menu (€310) with 25 creations, Madrid, Madrid, Madrid Menu (€240) with 23 creations, and Essence Menu... €190 for Thursday and Friday lunch.

claim: Ramón Freixa Atelier (Barrio de Salamanca, Calle Velázquez 24) was awarded two Michelin stars in the 2026 Guide only five months after opening, with a 10-seat U-shaped counter and Origen tasting menu at €230.
quote: Atelier is a kind of clandestine speakeasy within the larger Tradición... only 10 diners... two Michelin Stars in the 2026 Guide... The Origen menu costs 230 euros.

claim: DSTAgE (chef Diego Guerrero, Chueca) is a 2-star industrial-loft tasting destination with DSTAGE (15 courses) and DENJOY (18 courses) menus ranging €175–€220, also holding a Michelin Green Star.
quote: DSTAgE offers two tasting menus: DSTAGE, with 15 courses; and DENJOY, with 18 courses... The menu ranges from €175 to €220... awarded the Green Star in 2025.

claim: Saddle (Chamberí, C. de Amador de los Ríos 6) is a one-star restaurant in the elegant classic-luxury idiom on the site of the historic Jockey, with a classic-contemporary à la carte plus tasting menu and €€€€ pricing.
quote: Saddle replicates the philosophy and excellence of luxury restaurants from days gone by... C. de Amador de los Ríos, 6... Chamberí district.

claim: La Tasquería (chef Javi Estévez, relocated 2024 to Chamberí near Nuevos Ministerios) holds one Michelin star for haute-cuisine offal — a casual, accessible €€€ counter-to-table format.
quote: Javi Estévez revolutionized Madrid's culinary scene by elevating humble offal to the realms of haute-cuisine... In March 2024, the restaurant moved from the Salamanca neighbourhood to Chamberí.

claim: Corral de la Morería Gastronómico (Centro, La Latina) is the world's only Michelin-starred flamenco venue; chef David García runs an 8-seat Basque-leaning tasting room with the Compás menu around €120, separate from the larger tablao show (€48).
quote: Corral de la Morería is the only flamenco venue in the world to hold a Michelin star... only four tables for no more than eight guests... Gastronomic Tasting Menu is priced at 120 EUR.

claim: Madrid's 24 one-star houses include traditional (A'Barra, Desde 1911, Santerra), Japanese (Yugo The Bunker, Toki, Sen Omakase, Ugo Chan), Latin-influenced (Quimbaya — Colombian, Chispa Bistró, Èter) and plant-forward (El Invernadero, Pabú) options spanning every major neighborhood.
quote: Includes: Ricardo Sanz Wellington (Japanese), A'Barra (Technical cuisine), Gaytán, Yugo (Japanese haute cuisine), La Tasquería (Offal), El Invernadero (Vegetable-focused), Saddle, Quimbaya (Colombian), RavioXO (Pasta), Ugo Chan.

claim: Booking lead times in Madrid scale with stars: DiverXO ~12 weeks with deposit; two-star houses (Coque, DSTAgE, Ramón Freixa, Kabuki Wellington) 4–6 weeks; one-stars (Saddle, La Tasquería, Sen Omakase) 3–4 weeks, all best booked direct or via TheFork.
quote: DiverXO runs 12 weeks ahead with strict deposit rules, while the two-Michelin-starred restaurants run 4-6 weeks ahead. One-star Michelin restaurants run 3-4 weeks ahead.

claim: In the 2026 Michelin Guide ceremony, EMi (Nordic-Korean fusion) and Èter (Latin-influenced) were the notable new one-star awards in Madrid, while Ramón Freixa Atelier was the headline two-star promotion.
quote: EMi and Èter in Madrid are newly Starred restaurants in the 2026 Michelin Guide... EMi offers a subtle fusion of Nordic and Korean influences in an intimate format.
